implementation_notes: Java's canonical scatter runs through the persistence and transport layers: a new domain field means the entity, the JPA mapping, the DTO, the mapper, the builder, the fixture and the API doc. The structural fix is to stop duplicating the type at the boundary — either map at the edge and keep one domain type (which is what an anti-corruption layer is for), or accept the DTO and generate the rest. Lombok and Java records remove the boilerplate half of the scatter but not the type duplication, so the change still lands in several files; the honest fix there is to reduce the number of distinct types carrying the same data.
idiom_name: add field to entity, DTO, mapper, builder and test fixture
pitfalls: `@JsonProperty` on a field that no DTO carries is invisible in the diff and silently drops the field from the API.
Lombok `@Data` hides the change in the accessor generator, so a domain change does not visibly touch the DTO at all.
Flyway/Liquibase migrations pin the schema, so the scatter also crosses into SQL and must be versioned separately.
